findings.criterion: Tasks 1 and 16; Task 16 and Reachability acceptance criteria
findings.rationale: The required success order—Engine exit 0, immediate proof-gated teardown, then close-out/commit—is impossible with the current Engine. engine-git.ps1:633-648 requires main HEAD and working files to equal the integration tip before teardown. engine-git-test.ps1:370-374 explicitly proves teardown fails before close-out updates main HEAD. apex-engine.ps1:1398-1400 consequently instructs commit before teardown. Engine changes are a non-goal and its files are outside scope, so T16 cannot pass as written. The simpler supported structure is close-out/owner commit before teardown.

findings.criterion: Task 16; File Operations; Scope acceptance criterion
findings.rationale: T16 labels the smoke as “files: none; read-only smoke evidence,” but a real Engine run plus Scribe/docs/commit close-out necessarily writes another repository and creates build artifacts. Permissions authorize only listed modify/delete rows, Create is none, and line 200 requires that no other file was written. A separately authorized smoke spec could resolve this, but the target and nested-scope mechanism are not specified; the builder cannot satisfy both T16 and the scope criterion.

“Read engine-state status and diagnosis on every return” is not implementable without an Engine change. apex-engine.ps1 can exit 1 before creating any state—for example invalid/missing absolute inputs at 1483-1484 or root/wrapper validation at 1734-1745—and its no-state catch prints only an Engine-refused message at 1765. The task must permit a pre-state refusal route or add an Engine producing mechanism.

The spec presents Engine eligibility as ending at xhigh and routes max/ultra manually, but engine-plan.ps1:535 and 644-647 accepts max and ultra; only the automatic retry ladder stops at xhigh (apex-engine.ps1:955-957). Planning should decide whether this is merely a host-routing convention or a true Engine eligibility rule. The latter currently has no enforcement mechanism.

findings.criterion: Task 3 done-when versus Task 3 acceptance criterion
findings.rationale: The task says “all Engine-refusal classes are explicit,” while it names five manual-path classes and the acceptance criterion checks only those five. engine-plan.ps1:568-772 has many additional refusals, including validator failure, malformed manifests, repo mismatch, dirty paths, and missing verify contracts. Duplicating every diagnosis would be large and brittle; planning should clarify that the five static eligibility exclusions are enumerated while other refusals route by durable diagnosis.

The referenced references/spec-contract.md does not exist anywhere in C:/Users/User/apex or C:/Users/User/.claude. The current validator still passes, but reviewers and builders cannot consult the stated governing contract; the pointer or intended contract location needs resolution.
